attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 18 Ιουλίου εκάστου έτους», the same day the folder's Romanian row already carries, and the man is the folder's own: the son of Theocletus, which is the kinship clause this folder's display name keeps. He is not `hyacinth-the-chamberlain`, who stands on another day. The Greek page adds his mother's name, Theonilla; his homeland, Amastris on the Euxine, and the bishop of it in those years, Heraclides; the raising of a dead child when he was three years old by calling on the name of Christ; the cutting down of a fruit tree the idolaters were worshipping, which is what got him arrested; the governor's name, Kastrinsios; the beating, the tearing out of his teeth, his being dragged out of the city with ropes and wounded with sharpened reeds, and his death in prison. It gives no year at all, so nothing is proposed for `dates`. The page's etymology box retells the Greek myth of Hyacinth and Apollo; that is the site's note on the name and nothing of it is recorded here as his. No asterisk and no «Δεν είναι διασταυρωμένη» sentence. The page prints no hymn.
